The archive manager (archive.html) opens, creates and edits archives: browse folders, preview files, extract files, add files and folders, create folders, rename, delete and convert between formats.

Format Open Save
ZIP (also .jar, .docx, .xlsx, .odt, .epub, .apk, .whl and other ZIP-based files) yes, incl. ZIP64 yes (up to 4 GiB and 65,535 entries)
TAR yes (ustar, pax, GNU long names, symbolic links) yes
TAR.GZ / TGZ yes yes
GZ (a single compressed file) yes yes
7z yes yes (without encryption)
RAR (versions 4 and 5) yes – (save as 7z or ZIP)
TAR.XZ, TAR.BZ2, TAR.ZST, TAR.LZMA yes –
ISO, CAB, DEB, RPM, CPIO, AR, XAR yes –

7z, RAR and the further formats are read with libarchive (built into the application). The whole archive is unpacked when it is opened, so large archives need as much memory as their content. Save on a format that can only be read opens Save as with 7z suggested. Encrypted 7z and RAR archives cannot be opened (a message says so; encrypted ZIP archives are supported, see below), and a single compressed file without an archive inside (e.g. notes.txt.xz) cannot be opened either.

Opening and creating

  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens an archive. You can also drop an archive onto the window while no archive is open.
  • New starts an empty ZIP archive. Dropping files onto the window while nothing is open also starts a new archive.
  • In Chrome/Edge on the desktop the start page lists recently used archives.

Browsing

  • The list shows the content of the current folder: name, size (for folders the number of items), packed size (ZIP) and modification date. Click a column header to sort.
  • Double-click (on phones: tap) a folder to open it. ↑, Backspace or the path above the list go back.
  • Double-click (tap) a file to preview it: text, images, audio and video. Download in the preview saves the file.

Selecting

Click selects one item, Ctrl+click adds or removes items, Shift+click selects a range, Ctrl+A selects all items of the folder. The checkboxes select items too (on phones and tablets they are the way to select).

Extracting

  • Extract extracts the selected items, Extract all the whole current folder.
  • A single file is downloaded directly.
  • In Chrome/Edge on the desktop you choose a target folder; the files are written into it with their subfolders.
  • In Firefox and on Android, several files are downloaded together as one ZIP file.

✓ Test checks the whole archive: every file is decompressed and, for ZIP archives, compared with its stored checksum (CRC-32). The result lists damaged files with the reason; nothing is extracted or changed. Encrypted files need the password.

Editing

Function Description
Add files / Add folder adds files or a whole folder into the current folder; you can also drop files and folders onto the window
New folder creates a folder and lets you enter its name
Rename (F2) renames the selected file or folder
Delete (Del) removes the selected items from the archive

Existing files with the same name are replaced after a confirmation.

Undo (↶, Ctrl+Z) and redo (↷, Ctrl+Y) work for adding, renaming, deleting and new folders.

Open with… (toolbar or preview) opens the selected file in another application of the suite; saving there replaces the file in the archive (undoable). Save the archive afterwards.

Saving

  • Save (Ctrl+S) writes the archive in its format: directly into the opened file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android (replace the original file with it).
  • Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) asks for the file name and the format (ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, GZ). This converts an archive, for example a .tar.gz into a .zip. A GZ file holds exactly one file.
  • Compression in the status bar sets the compression of new and changed files: Store, Fastest, Normal, Maximum. Unchanged files of an opened ZIP archive are copied as they are, so saving is fast.

Encrypted ZIP archives

Encrypted files are marked with 🔒 (the tooltip names the method). Previewing, extracting or opening such a file asks for the password; it is remembered until another archive is opened. Both methods in use are supported: AES (WinZip AES, 128/192/256 bit, used by 7-Zip, WinZip and others) and ZipCrypto (the old method that Windows can open without extra software).

  • After you entered the password of an archive, files you add or change are encrypted the same way when saving (shown as 🔒 in the status bar). Unchanged files are kept as they are.
  • Save as offers the encryption of a ZIP archive: none, AES-256 (recommended) or ZipCrypto (weak; choose it only for the Windows Explorer), with the password entered twice. All files that are not encrypted yet are then encrypted; files that already were keep their password. Choosing "none" saves new and changed files without encryption.
  • File names and the list of files are not encrypted in ZIP archives, only the contents.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

On phones and tablets

The toolbar can be scrolled sideways. The list shows name and size; tap a folder to open it and a file to preview it, use the checkboxes to select.
